source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Chemistry (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring; stems restated in our own wording, no solution content from the source book appears here, by policy. VSAQ 25 entries over 19 printed numbers (Q9 five parts, Q14 and Q16 two parts each), SAQ 9 over 8 numbers (Q26 two parts; Q27 repeats Q20 verbatim), LAQ 3 over 2 numbers (Q29 two parts), PROBLEM 4 (the book prints the block as 'INTEXT SOLVED QUESTIONS', NCERT-numbered 8.1–8.4). The left margin of printed pages 100, 101 and 102 is cropped in the scan, so the leading digit or asterisk of Q12, Q17, Q18 and Q27 is partly cut off.

questions.stem: Describe how the oxidation states vary across the group-13 elements from boron to thallium.
Give the reason for the higher stability of TlCl.
Explain why BF₃ acts as a Lewis acid.
State whether boric acid is a protic acid, and explain.
Describe what happens when boric acid is heated.
Describe the shapes of BF₃ and BH₄⁻ and give the hybridisation of boron in each of these species.
Explain why the atomic radius of Ga is smaller than that of Al.
Explain the inert pair effect.
Write the balanced equation for the reaction BF₃ + LiH →.
questions.notes: Five printed parts (a)–(e) under one stem 'Write the balanced equations for'. The book's answer adds an unasked part (f) for the heating of B₂H₆·2NH₃.

State the hybridisation of boron in diborane and in borazine [B₃N₃H₆].

The standard electrode potential E° for Al³⁺/Al is −1.66 V and that for Tl³⁺/Tl is +1.26 V. Predict the formation of the M³⁺ ion in solution for each metal and compare the electropositive character of the two metals.
questions.notes: Printed label 8.1 in the block headed 'INTEXT SOLVED QUESTIONS'. The book prints the potential symbol as E⁻ (typo for E°).
